idiom_name: await Verify(actual) - .received. vs .verified. artefacts with DiffEngine
implementation_notes: Verify is the de-facto .NET snapshot tool and supplies the whole loop: the test returns await Verify(value), Verify serializes the result into a .received. file beside a committed .verified. file, compares the two and fails with a diff; approval means promoting the received file, done through DiffEngine's tray, the ReSharper/Rider plugins, Verify.Terminal or a plain file rename. It binds to xUnit v3, NUnit, MSTest, TUnit, Fixie and Expecto, so the hand-written comparator disappears. Scrubbers and VerifySettings replace ad-hoc normalization; add a diff tool and exclude *.received.* from source control.
pitfalls: .received. files get committed by accident and .verified. files get approved unseen; add both to repository hygiene rules and keep CI unable to write them.
Volatile values (guids, timestamps, machine paths) must be removed with scrubbers or VerifySettings, otherwise the snapshot flakes on every machine.
Serializing a whole object graph pins fields you never meant to promise; use VerifySettings to select the observable projection.

variants.name: Hand-written golden files with xUnit
variants.idiom_name: xUnit [Theory] + committed files under TestData/ compared with Assert.Equal
variants.implementation_notes: Without a snapshot library the loop is hand-written: capture the subject's output as a string or byte array, read the committed file from a TestData directory (resolved relative to the test project, not the build output), compare with Assert.Equal so xUnit renders the diff, and gate rewriting behind an environment variable or an explicit [Fact(Skip)] recorder. Choose this when bringing a dependency into a regulated or offline build is harder than writing thirty lines, or when the artefact is produced by an external process the test only wraps.
pitfalls: TestData files must be copied to the test output (or referenced by project-relative path); otherwise every run reads an empty or missing file and the assertion is vacuous.
Assert.Equal on multi-megabyte strings truncates the diff, so failures are unreadable; compare line by line and print the first difference.
Environment-variable update paths are easy to leave enabled in a pipeline; assert the flag is unset on CI.
